use_case: Dynamic ticket pricing: changes the price of each price level as demand changes, within floors and ceilings, for reserved-seat events at 27 group venues and for 310 opt-in client tenants
business_owner: VP Product, Pricing and Access (product); VP Ticketing and Box Office (group venues)
vendor_or_model: In-house demand forecasting model in the TVOP pricing module
data_categories: Aggregate sales velocity, seats remaining, days to event, page views, queue size, floor and ceiling settings; no patron-level data (tested)
consequential_decision_category: None (same price for every buyer at a given time); re-tier High if patron-level data is ever used
human_in_the_loop: Group venues: auto-apply within floors and ceilings today. Conditions: accessible levels removed from auto-apply; artist caps as ceilings; approval queue for changes over 25% in 24 hours. Clients set their own settings; product safeguard for accessible levels by default
applicable_laws: 16 CFR 464.2, 464.3 (N71-R05); 15 U.S.C. 45(a) (N71-R05); 28 CFR 36.302(f)(3); state surveillance-pricing laws (for example Connecticut PA 26-64) not expected to apply while no personal data is used; counsel reviews client deployments
status: In production; continue with conditions (conditions due 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-30)

use_case: Bot detection and virtual queue: scores each session in high-demand on-sales and allows, challenges, or blocks it; randomizes queue position
vendor_or_model: In-house risk scoring model in the TVOP access module
data_categories: Device and browser signals, network address and type, request timing, account age; session records kept 30 days
consequential_decision_category: None (access to one on-sale; box office and phone remain open)
human_in_the_loop: Automated per-session decisions; humans handle appeals and releases (logged) and review linked-account evidence before cancelling any order
applicable_laws: BOTS Act 15 U.S.C. 45c (protects ticket issuers and their agents); Fla. Stat. 817.36(5); 15 U.S.C. 45(a) posted limits and privacy statements (N71-R05); 28 CFR 36.302(f)(1)(ii) same stages of sale
status: In production (about 1,900 protected on-sales a year); continue with conditions

use_case: Hotel revenue management: recommends and publishes room rates to all channels
data_categories: Aggregate bookings and stay history, competitor rates, event calendar; no individual guest data
human_in_the_loop: Rates published automatically within hotel floors; weekly review added as a condition
status: In production; register and weekly review by 2026-12-31

use_case: Patron propensity and segmentation models for cross-division marketing on the patron data platform
data_categories: Ticket, hotel, dining, and streaming purchase history (group customers only); no identity document numbers after POAM-024
human_in_the_loop: Marketing staff choose campaigns; no automated decision about eligibility for any service
applicable_laws: 15 U.S.C. 45(a)(1) (N51-R01); N51-R03 CCPA (opt-out of sale and sharing; ADMT rules cover significant decisions only); client agreements (no client data)

data_categories: Viewing history and preferences of subscribers
human_in_the_loop: Subscribers choose what to watch; recommendations labeled

use_case: Face-based express entry pilot at 2 Florida amphitheaters: matches an enrolled patron's face at the gate to the ticket holder
vendor_or_model: Face matching vendor (camera kiosks and cloud matching)
data_categories: Face templates computed from enrollment selfies and gate camera images; ticket and account data; about 38,000 enrolled patrons
consequential_decision_category: None in the rubric categories; access to a venue; group standard tiers it High because it processes biometric data
human_in_the_loop: Gate staff admit any patron by ticket scan if matching fails; opting out never blocks entry
applicable_laws: Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI) and 501.702 definitions (worked example; whether face templates from camera images are biometric data is unsettled, so the group treats them as biometric data); 15 U.S.C. 45(a) (N51-R01); Florida Digital Bill of Rights does not apply (controller test not met)
status: Pilot since 2026-05; new enrollments paused; conditions due 2026-12-31

use_case: Generative customer support assistant for patrons on the ticketing site and app
vendor_or_model: Hosted large language model service from a third-party model provider (no-training, zero-retention terms)
data_categories: Patron questions; order details after sign-in; conversation logs kept 90 days
consequential_decision_category: None (refund and exchange decisions made by staff)
human_in_the_loop: Assistant answers and drafts; refunds, exchanges, and account changes go to human agents
applicable_laws: 15 U.S.C. 45(a) (N51-R01); disclosure of AI interaction; client agreements for client-branded support
status: In production; continue with monthly sampling

use_case: Payment fraud and card-testing scoring in payment orchestration
vendor_or_model: In-house model with acquirer risk signals
data_categories: Transaction attributes, device signals, velocity; card data stays in the CDE
consequential_decision_category: None (a declined payment can be retried or bought at the box office)
human_in_the_loop: Automated declines above a threshold; patron appeals handled by client support
applicable_laws: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (N71-R04) for CDE handling; 15 U.S.C. 45(a) (N51-R01)

use_case: Enterprise generative AI assistant pilot for 3,000 workforce users
human_in_the_loop: Users review outputs; prohibited for pricing decisions and Restricted data
applicable_laws: POL-05 4.7; 15 U.S.C. 45(a) (N51-R01) for any customer-facing use
